source.title: Scaling Laws of Machine Learning for Optimal Power Flow
source.authors: Xin-Yi Liu; Xuan He; Yi-Ze Chen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to supervised machine learning for optimal power flow, a different task from language-model pretraining, and reports its own data- and compute-scaling results.
record.gate_note: The paper tests power-law relationships for OPF prediction error and other performance metrics, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. Only V5 is treated as tested, as a test of whether a power-law form carries over to a different training task. The DNN-versus-PINN comparison and results across network sizes are not rows because they do not measure a data- or compute-scaling relationship.
record.test_reason: Fits power laws of held-out prediction error (MAE) against training-set size and training FLOPs for small supervised MLPs on optimal power flow. This is a new training regime and setting for the power-law form (V5). It does not touch language-model loss, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say OPF prediction MAE follows predictable power laws in data and compute, while constraint feasibility (especially reactive power, and DCOPF overall) improves much more slowly and is the deployment bottleneck. They also claim OPF compute exponents are 3.8–5x steeper than Kaplan's language-model exponent.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised DNN and PINN experiments on OPF, using prediction MAE and constraint violations rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy. The study cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as related work.
record.method_sensitivity: Compute-fit R2 differs between DCOPF and ACOPF; the paper also reports differing best depths for the two problems (3 layers for DCOPF and 2 for ACOPF), though that is not a language-model architecture test.

fits_no_version.finding: Constraint-violation metrics scale inconsistently with data. DCOPF violations stay flat. ACOPF Pg and branch violations fall roughly as power laws, while Qg violations barely move (exponent -0.03).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling of feasibility or constraint metrics diverges from scaling of training-error metrics in physics-constrained regression.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting
record.problems: The compute power-law fits have modest R2 values (0.259, 0.586, and 0.632); the paper reports no error bars or confidence intervals. The reported metrics and task differ from language-model pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: Table II's DNN-versus-PINN comparisons and Table III's network-size comparisons are not data- or compute-scaling fits. The paper also discusses architecture-specific depth optima, which do not test the listed language-model versions.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss is measured.
No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs is tested.
No language-model compute-optimal split is fitted. The OPF IsoLoss frontier (Fig. 2) is not quantified as exponents.
No language-model test. Depth optima for OPF MLPs (3 layers for DCOPF, 2 for ACOPF) are only described qualitatively.
Only small MLPs on DC/ACOPF regression at one system size (118-bus) are tested. No image, video, repeated-data or fine-tuning regimes.

missing.what: PINN MAE and violations at 1K vs 40K samples. DCOPF PINN MAE does not improve (4.56 to 4.73). ACOPF PINN Pg MAE improves (4.03 to 2.29). The abstract claims power laws for PINNs, but no PINN fit is reported.
Compute-optimal frontier: IsoLoss contours over FLOPs and parameters, with an efficiency frontier. No exponents are given.
missing.versions: V5 (OPF analogue of V3; not an LM test)

record.verdict_notes: The label array's third entry has a key typo in the source draft. Its row_ids should be empty: the verdict rests on Table II text. The Kaplan exponent comparison (-0.050) is a cited value, not a row. The abstract gives R2 = 0.9 for the ACOPF data fit, versus 0.992 in Section III-B. Tables III (system size) and II (DNN vs PINN) are correctly left out of rows, except for PINN data scaling, listed under missing.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy or its scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small language-model runs are used to predict the loss of larger runs.
The study does not find a parameter-count and token-count allocation that minimizes language-model loss at fixed compute.
It does not test language-model loss at fixed parameter count while varying depth, width, or other architecture details.
Tests supervised OPF prediction and feasibility metrics, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer; it does not measure pretraining cross-entropy.
No downstream-task performance is related to language-model scale or pretraining loss.
The paper does not investigate setup-dependent fitting choices or disagreements among language-model scaling laws.

rows.operation_detail: Measured generator-limit violation across training dataset sizes.
rows.value: The paper states that violations remain flat across all data scales; Table I reports 641.9 MW at 0.1K and 640.4 MW at 40K.
rows.note: The paper attributes the lack of improvement to errors from the DCOPF linear approximation.
rows.check: DCOPF constraint violation is a feasibility metric, not the held-out error or loss whose power-law form V5 names. Move it to fits_no_version.

rows.value: The paper states that violations remain flat across all data scales; Table I reports 89.4% at 0.1K and 88.5% at 40K.

rows.value: Pg Vio(D) = 1.93 · D^-0.207; 0.39 MW at 40K samples
rows.note: The paper reports an 87% improvement and says this metric is more sensitive to optimization dynamics than accuracy.
rows.check: Feasibility metric, not loss or error. The fit's R2 is 0.600 (eq. 11).

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured reactive-generator-limit violation across training dataset sizes.
rows.value: Qg Vio(D) = 27.6 · D^-0.030; Table I reports 25.7 MVar at 40K samples.
rows.note: The paper characterizes reactive-power constraints as a persistent bottleneck.
rows.check: Feasibility metric. The exponent -0.030 with R2 0.700 is essentially flat, and Table I is non-monotone (24.9 at 10K, 25.7 at 40K). Absent, not partial.

rows.subject: DNN
